newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metro to raise stake in Smart before IPO.
newsitem.headline: Metro to raise stake in Smart before IPO.

text.p: Metro Pacific Corp officials said on Friday the company would raise its stake in cellular phone firm Smart Communications Inc to more than 50 percent from the present 35 percent.
"It is expected that Smart will become a subsidiary of Metro Pacific," Metro Pacific vice chairman Ricardo Pascua told reporters and analysts after Metro's stockholders' meeting.
Pascua said Metro Pacific would buy Smart shares held by First Pacific Co Ltd which currently holds about 35 percent by issuing new Metro Pacific shares to First Pacific.
Metro Pacific is the Philippine flagship company of the Hong Kong-based First Pacific.
The valuation of the share swap has not yet been established.
Metro executive director Seumas Gallacher said the stake would be raised before Smart launches its initial public offering in July.
The issue is being offered to foreign investors. Under Philippine law, foreign owners are limited to 40 percent of telecommunication companies.
Smart president Orlando Vea said his company posted a 74 million peso income before tax in the first quarter of the year.
It is expected to post at least 700 million pesos in net income this year, up from 254 million pesos last year.
